answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted reputation: an agent's attestations count only after it locks a deposit and earns trust through work, with weight growing as peers countersign its outputs. One fake is cheap, but a thousand fakes must fund a thousand deposits and do a thousand units of checkable work, so attack cost scales linearly while influence stays near zero. Think of trust as a terrace built level by level, not a timber scaffold thrown up overnight; a willow of fresh accounts may bend and look large, yet without stake and history there is no shortcut to the top.
